You are working for an event catering company that has been hired to plan a corporate team building event menu for 30 people. Your task is to design a complete catering plan and get client approval.

Use the HowToCook recipe database to browse recipes across different categories. Select at least 8 dishes to create a full catering menu with appetizers, main courses, and at least one dessert or soup. Choose recipes that would work well for a corporate team building setting serving 30 people.

Create an Excel workbook called Catering_Plan.xlsx in your workspace with two sheets. The first sheet must be named Menu and include the columns Dish_Name, Category (use values like Appetizer, Main_Course, Soup, or Dessert), Servings_For_30 (the number of servings needed to feed the 30 guests, which is approximately 30 — one serving per guest — scaled up from the recipe's default serving count), Prep_Time_Minutes (estimated preparation time as a number), and Estimated_Cost_USD (estimated cost in US dollars as a number, estimate $3-8 per serving for most dishes). Write all numeric values (Servings_For_30, Prep_Time_Minutes, Estimated_Cost_USD, and any quantities) as literal numbers, not Excel formulas. The Menu sheet should have at least 8 data rows. The second sheet must be named Ingredients and include the columns Dish_Name, Ingredient, Quantity_For_30_People, and Unit.

Create a Word document called Catering_Proposal.docx in your workspace. Include an executive summary describing the event and your catering approach, a menu overview section listing all selected dishes with brief descriptions, and a preparation timeline section describing when each category of dish will be prepared on the event day.

Create a Google Form called "Menu Approval Survey" with questions to collect client feedback on the proposed menu. Include at least three questions: one asking the client to rate overall menu satisfaction, one asking which dishes they want to confirm or remove, and one asking for any special dietary requirements or additional notes.

Send an email to client@corporate.com with subject "Catering Proposal for Team Building Event" that summarizes the proposed menu and mentions that the Excel plan, Word proposal, and feedback form have been prepared.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Make one bounded category-discovery pass, select exactly eight suitable dishes covering appetizers, main courses, and at least one soup or dessert, and retrieve those eight recipe details with native-parallel calls. Freeze one eight-dish table and reuse it everywhere. Create `Catering_Plan.xlsx`, `Catering_Proposal.docx`, and the Form `Menu Approval Survey` as independent output branches. The workbook must use the exact two sheets and headers, literal numeric values, `Servings_For_30` values scaled to approximately 30, positive costs, and ingredient rows referencing the same dish names. Build the Word document with one bulk structured body containing the exact title, Executive Summary, Menu Overview, and Preparation Timeline and mentioning at least four exact selected dish names. Create the Form exactly once with these three explicit questions: `Rate the overall menu satisfaction from 1 to 5`; `Which dishes should we confirm or remove?`; and `List any special dietary requirements or additional notes`. Verify each deliverable once, then send exactly one email to `client@corporate.com` with subject `Catering Proposal for Team Building Event`.

CONTEXT: You are supporting an event catering company that is planning a corporate team-building event menu for 30 guests. Your job is READ-ONLY recipe research using the HowToCook MCP tools available to you (mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes, mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory, mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById, mcp_howtocook_recommendMeals, mcp_howtocook_whatToEat). Do not create, modify, or delete anything — only gather and report.

GOAL: Curate a 9-dish catering menu with this exact composition:
- 3 appetizers: light, starter-style dishes — cold vegetable plates / salads / 凉拌 dishes from the 素菜 category work well (or a suitable 早餐 finger food)
- 4 main courses: crowd-pleasing dishes from the 荤菜, 水产, and/or 主食 categories; include at least one rice or noodle staple dish, a mix of proteins (e.g., chicken, pork/beef, seafood), and at least one vegetable-forward main
- 1 soup: from the 汤 category
- 1 dessert: from the 甜品 category

Selection criteria: realistic to batch-cook for 30 people in a corporate catering setting, crowd-pleasing for a corporate audience, balanced variety, ingredients that are reasonably easy to source. Avoid 半成品加工 (semi-processed) recipes and overly exotic/specialty dishes.

METHOD: Browse categories with mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory (valid category values: 水产, 早餐, 调料, 甜品, 饮品, 荤菜, 半成品加工, 汤, 主食, 素菜). Shortlist candidates, then call mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById for EACH chosen dish to fetch full details (ingredients with quantities, steps, serving info).

REPORT BACK (this report is the deliverable — it will be used verbatim to build a catering spreadsheet, so numbers must be precise and complete):
For each of the 9 dishes:
1. Chinese name (exactly as it appears in the database) + a natural English translation
2. Recipe ID
3. Database category it came from
4. Menu role: Appetizer / Main_Course / Soup / Dessert
5. The recipe's default serving count (from recipe metadata or per-serving info) and the scale factor to reach 30 servings (30 ÷ default servings, e.g. recipe serves 3 → factor 10)
6. FULL ingredient list as a table with columns: Ingredient (Chinese + English) | Original quantity + unit | Scaled quantity for 30 people + unit. Do the scaling math yourself. If a quantity is vague (适量 / 少许 / to taste), give a realistic specific quantity and mark it "(est.)"
7. Number of cooking steps, any time info found, and your estimate of total prep+cook minutes for one normal batch
8. One-sentence English description of the dish suitable for a client-facing proposal

End with a compact summary table: # | English name | Chinese name | Role | Default servings | Scale factor | Est. minutes per batch.
Research HowToCook catering menu

TASK: Create a professional Word document at the EXACT path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-event-catering-excel-word/workspace/Catering_Proposal.docx

SUBJECT: A catering proposal from our event catering company to a corporate client (client@corporate.com) for a corporate team building event with 30 guests. The proposed menu is a 9-dish Chinese banquet-style buffet — 3 appetizers, 4 main courses, 1 soup, 1 dessert — with every dish scaled to 30 servings (one serving per guest). Estimated total food cost: USD 1,245 (about USD 41.50 per guest). Total active kitchen preparation across all dishes: roughly 670 minutes (~11 hours), organized into a make-ahead day and the event day.

REQUIRED STRUCTURE (use built-in Word heading styles so the document outline is clean):

1. Title (Heading 1): "Catering Proposal for Corporate Team Building Event", followed by a short info paragraph: "Prepared for: Corporate Client (client@corporate.com) | Event: Corporate Team Building Event | Guests: 30 | Service Style: Banquet Buffet"

2. Heading 1 "Executive Summary" — 2–3 well-written paragraphs covering: the event (30-guest corporate team building event) and our catering approach (a balanced nine-dish banquet buffet spanning appetizers, main courses, soup and dessert; every dish scaled to 30 servings so each guest enjoys a full portion of each dish; a deliberate mix of chicken, pork, seafood and vegetable-forward dishes; make-ahead-friendly cold appetizers, soup and dessert that keep event-day kitchen pressure low; transparent allergen labelling — the menu contains peanuts, shellfish, egg, soy and sesame, and every dish can be adapted or substituted for dietary needs), plus the headline numbers (total estimated food cost USD 1,245 ≈ USD 41.50 per guest; ~670 minutes of total preparation managed across a make-ahead day and event day).

3. Heading 1 "Menu Overview" — one short intro paragraph, then a bordered TABLE with a bold header row summarizing the full menu (10 rows including header). Columns: Dish | Category | Servings | Prep Time (min) | Est. Cost (USD). Rows:
- Smashed Cucumber Salad (凉拌黄瓜) | Appetizer | 30 | 40 | 90
- Chilled Enoki Mushroom Salad (凉拌金针菇) | Appetizer | 30 | 30 | 105
- Chilled Wood Ear Mushroom Salad (凉拌木耳) | Appetizer | 30 | 60 | 105
- Kung Pao Chicken (宫保鸡丁) | Main_Course | 30 | 120 | 180
- Mapo Tofu (麻婆豆腐) | Main_Course | 30 | 60 | 135
- Steamed Sea Bass with Ginger & Scallion (清蒸鲈鱼) | Main_Course | 30 | 75 | 225
- Yangzhou Fried Rice (扬州炒饭) | Main_Course | 30 | 90 | 150
- Sweet Corn & Pork Rib Soup (玉米排骨汤) | Soup | 30 | 120 | 120
- Baked Egg Tarts (烤蛋挞) | Dessert | 30 | 75 | 135
(You may show Category values as friendlier labels such as "Appetizer", "Main Course", "Soup", "Dessert" in this document.)
Then add a Heading 2 subsection per category, listing each dish as its own short paragraph with the dish name in BOLD followed by a brief description:
- Heading 2 "Appetizers":
  • Smashed Cucumber Salad (凉拌黄瓜) — a refreshingly crisp smashed-cucumber salad tossed in a garlic–vinegar–soy dressing; a light, palate-cleansing way to open the meal.
  • Chilled Enoki Mushroom Salad (凉拌金针菇) — silky chilled enoki mushrooms in a bright garlic–soy vinaigrette, finished with scallion and a whisper of chili oil.
  • Chilled Wood Ear Mushroom Salad (凉拌木耳) — crunchy chilled wood-ear mushrooms in a tangy black-vinegar dressing with fresh chili and garlic; a classic cold starter.
- Heading 2 "Main Courses":
  • Kung Pao Chicken (宫保鸡丁) — tender diced chicken stir-fried with roasted peanuts, scallions and dried chilies in the signature sweet-tangy Kung Pao glaze; an internationally beloved classic (contains peanuts; mildly spicy).
  • Mapo Tofu (麻婆豆腐) — silken tofu simmered in a fragrant, gently spiced pork-mince and garlic-chili sauce; the beloved Sichuan classic that pairs perfectly with rice.
  • Steamed Sea Bass with Ginger & Scallion (清蒸鲈鱼) — whole fresh sea bass steamed to delicate flakes with ginger and scallion, finished with hot oil and seasoned soy; an elegant banquet centerpiece.
  • Yangzhou Fried Rice (扬州炒饭) — wok-tossed fried rice with egg, shrimp, diced ham, sweet peas, carrot and corn; a colorful, universally loved staple.
- Heading 2 "Soup":
  • Sweet Corn & Pork Rib Soup (玉米排骨汤) — a slow-simmered clear soup of pork ribs, sweet corn and carrot; naturally sweet, comforting and warming for the whole table.
- Heading 2 "Dessert":
  • Baked Egg Tarts (烤蛋挞) — flaky, golden custard tarts baked fresh; creamy inside, crisp outside — the perfect sweet finish.

4. Heading 1 "Preparation Timeline" — a short intro paragraph explaining the kitchen workflow (make-ahead day plus event-day schedule with parallel stations), then a bordered timeline TABLE (bold header row) with columns Time | Activity, rows:
- Day before event | Procurement and make-ahead prep: soak dried wood-ear mushrooms, cook and chill rice for the fried rice, marinate Kung Pao chicken, bake egg tarts and chill
- Event day, T-5 hours | Soup: blanch pork ribs and start the Sweet Corn & Pork Rib Soup simmer; holds warm in steam kettles until service
- Event day, T-3 hours | Appetizers: smash and marinate cucumbers, blanch enoki and wood-ear mushrooms, dress and chill all three cold appetizers
- Event day, T-2 hours | Main courses: stir-fry Kung Pao Chicken in batches and prepare Mapo Tofu; hold hot
- Event day, T-90 minutes | Steamed Sea Bass: steam fish in 3–4 steamer cycles and keep warm for plating
- Event day, T-45 minutes | Yangzhou Fried Rice: final wok-frying in batches using the pre-chilled rice
- Event day, T-30 minutes | Final assembly: season the soup, plate appetizers and dessert, set up the buffet line and hot-hold the mains
- Service | Buffet opens; kitchen team replenishes dishes and maintains safe holding temperatures
Then one short paragraph per category summarizing WHY it is scheduled that way (e.g., cold appetizers are make-ahead and served chilled; soup benefits from a long simmer and holds well; mains are cooked closest to service for freshness; dessert is baked the day before and re-plated).

5. Heading 1 "Next Steps" — a short closing paragraph asking the client to complete the "Menu Approval Survey" Google Form (rate overall satisfaction, confirm or remove dishes, and flag special dietary requirements). Once approved, we will lock procurement and finalize event-day logistics; allergen accommodations and substitutions are available on request.

STYLE: clean, professional, client-facing. Use built-in heading styles, bold dish names in the menu overview paragraphs, bordered tables with bold header rows. Do not invent extra dishes, do not change any of the numbers above, no footnotes needed.

VERIFICATION (required before finishing): use get_document_outline / get_document_info to confirm the document exists and contains the required sections and tables. REPORT BACK: the file path, the heading outline, and confirmation that both tables (menu summary and timeline) are present.
